title: Foundation 5: rebuild bootstrap capability inventory as a consumer of accepted identities
description:
Successor to eshyra-o9bd.19.5.1 (PR #477, DESIGN_INVALIDATED). Blocked on
Foundation 4, and transitively on Foundations 1 and 3.

PREMISE CHANGE (why this exists): PRs #475/#476/#477 reached DESIGN_INVALIDATED
after repeatedly producing NEW defect classes following material contract changes
and fresh full reviews. The shared root cause was not implementation quality: in
all three, unsettled concepts were GENERALIZED ACROSS THE CORPUS before their
trust boundaries had been proven by a small number of concrete
source-to-execution examples. Successor work inverts that order.

GOAL: rebuild the bootstrap capability inventory as a CONSUMER of accepted
obligation, finding, and evidence identities — never as the place those
identities are invented. #477 invented its own incompatible obligation identity,
its own evidence taxonomy, and its own absence proof, none of which survived.

It MAY remain non-authoritative, but it must be honest, exact enough to guide
decomposition, and MECHANICALLY RECONCILABLE with the future authoritative
ledger (eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12).

SALVAGE AS-IS from #477: the corrected historical eshyra-2n1t reconciliation, and
the distinction between narrow child completion and overstated umbrella closure —
that analysis was accepted by review and is independent of the invalidated
evidence framework. It should be EXTRACTED so it does not die with the ledger.
SALVAGE AFTER EXTRACTION: candidate capability primitive names; ownership
candidates; the identification of primitives invisible from current pack
projection.
acceptance_criteria:
• The inventory consumes obligation, finding and evidence identities defined elsewhere; it invents none.
• The eshyra-2n1t historical reconciliation is preserved intact and independently reviewable.
• Non-authoritative status is explicit, and the artifact is mechanically reconcilable with eshyra-o9bd.19.5.12.
• No resolver claims more than its evidence proves.
